entry.title: This month in CSSWG (August 2026)
entry.content:
This month in CSSWG

This is an in-progress August snapshot, covering the mirror through August 27. The month has been unusually rich in author-facing design work: customizable form controls moved from a broad default-styling debate into concrete UA rules; Selectors gained a narrowly defined class-prefix syntax; and native mixins shed several pieces of syntax while gaining private variables. The group also opened new design space for 2D gradients and sticky scroll animations, while treating masonry reading order and line clamping as accessibility questions rather than layout details alone.

Notable this month

  • Customizable <select> moves from “styleable” to usable by default (#14256)
    • Background: Apple proposed that appearance: base controls should be production-usable before authors add CSS, backed by a survey of design systems. The proposal covered spacing, rounded corners, typography, icons, picker sizing, colors, shadows, and animation rather than treating each default in isolation.
    • Why it matters: customizable <select> is becoming a real authoring surface, but a bare primitive still leaves every design system to rediscover overflow, writing-mode, accessibility, and disabled-state rules. Better defaults reduce that burden; overly opinionated defaults create more CSS to undo and can become dated.
    • Summary: the joint meeting did not adopt the full visual proposal. Jen Simmons argued that polished defaults reduced one example from 66 to 28 author CSS lines and protected low-budget sites from missing edge cases (minutes); una and others warned that “timeless” styling is impossible and animations or shadows are expensive to reverse. The work was split into testable pieces. The picker now uses max-block-size: 100dvb with safe overflow alignment (#14172 resolution); traditional <select> markup gets a wrapper, subsequently named ::field-content, so long labels can clip without pushing out the picker icon (#14323 resolution, rename); and selected text now inherits overflow controls (#14255 resolution). Whether ::field-content matches under appearance: auto is still open. Internal icons are excluded from the accessibility tree (#14316 resolution), while input, select, and option gained block-axis centering, with checkbox/radio compatibility still to be checked (#14319 resolution).
    • Related: #14249, #14250, #14254, #14317, Anchor Positioning
  • A narrowly defined class-prefix selector lands (#10001)
    • Background: utility frameworks, icon libraries, and author conventions commonly encode a family in classes such as pt-6, bi-alarm, or btn-primary. Today, sharing rules across that family requires another class, generated selector lists, or the awkward [class^=…], [class*=…] pattern.
    • Why it matters: the new dot-identifier-hyphen-wildcard form lets a library target the common behavior of every hyphen-separated class in a family without enumerating it. It directly affects Tailwind/Bootstrap-style APIs, icon sets, and BEM-like naming, but also risks blessing one naming convention and complicating selector matching.
    • Summary: the group accepted the proposed class-selector form, limited specifically to a hyphen-separated prefix (resolution); arbitrary wildcard prefixes remain out. The draft followed on August 18, but public review reopened the design rationale. Critics argued that the syntax privileges utility frameworks, implies namespace semantics that HTML class tokens do not have, and may match BEM classes unexpectedly; proponents answered that the proposal targets an established, otherwise costly pattern rather than general substring matching. Even the boundary remains live: #14291 asks whether a trailing hyphen alone matches, and whether a double-hyphen BEM class belongs to the family.
    • Related: #14224, #14289, #14371
  • Native mixins converge on @mixin + @private, with call-site evaluation (#14243)
    • Background: the draft had accumulated overlapping constructs: @mixin and @macro, an @result wrapper, and pseudo-private custom-property conventions. A meta discussion treated these as one authoring-model problem rather than independent syntax bikesheds.
    • Why it matters: this is the difference between a feature that merely copies declarations and one that can support reusable component libraries without variable-name collisions. Fewer constructs make native mixins easier to learn; private variables and predictable units make them safer to compose.
    • Summary: the August 4 F2F resolved to keep @mixin, drop @macro, remove @result, and put hygienically rewritten custom properties in an @private block nested inside a style rule (four resolutions). A fresh objection asked to retain @macro as a Sass-like selector-extension feature, but the issue was closed because that behavior was never part of the construct; selector extension would be separate (#14387). A later resolution fixed a subtler surprise: function arguments, defaults, locals, and results are all evaluated where the function is called, so 1em, random(), and other context-dependent values do not change meaning merely because an argument is typed (#14338 resolution).
    • Related: #14004, #13727, #14212
  • 2D gradients: mesh compatibility research pushes CSS toward freeform-gradient() (#7648)
    • Background: the web can fake soft 2D color fields by layering radial gradients or drawing into Canvas/WebGL, but cannot express a true mesh/freeform gradient as a CSS image. The thread distinguishes grid-based mesh gradients with Bézier-controlled patches from freeform gradients authored as colored points.
    • Why it matters: a CSS image function would make designer-style color meshes responsive, animatable, and themeable without shipping raster assets or custom rendering code. The choice of primitive also determines whether authors get a short list of color points or an SVG/PDF-like matrix that usually needs tooling.
    • Summary: no resolution yet, but August materially changed the direction. Tests against SwiftUI and PDF exposed rendering artifacts and algorithm differences; rasterizing for PDF export was considered acceptable. Tab Atkins moved toward freeform-gradient() because its authoring model matches existing gradients—color plus position—while mesh syntax carries control points and color-smoothing choices (comment). Bramus' prototypes then showed that freeform output can map to tensor-product patches and PDF, reducing the compatibility objection. The remaining split is whether CSS should standardize the simple freeform surface first or define one structured model that can also cover full meshes.
    • Related: css-images-5
  • Masonry reading order enters explicit incubation, not normative shipping (#5675)
    • Background: display: grid-lanes can place visually adjacent cards far apart in DOM order. Earlier work agreed that masonry behaves more like Grid than Flexbox, but that did not supply a reading/focus order for irregular lanes.
    • Why it matters: visual masonry can otherwise send keyboard and assistive-technology users through a page in an order that no longer matches the layout. The problem grows when zoom or responsive reflow changes the number of lanes, so a plausible desktop ordering is not enough.
    • Summary: after proposals based on lane-by-lane traversal and “reading regions,” accessibility reviewers still found cases where focus could jump across columns or change under reflow. The group therefore chose incubation: add a per-lane value to reading-flow, and publish the broader algorithm only as an experimental informative appendix in Grid L3 while collecting feedback (resolution). Prototyping is encouraged, but public shipping must return to the WG. In parallel, Grid Lanes gained a shorthand direction, item-slack became fit-tolerance, and gap decorations were defined lane by lane; whether Grid and Grid Lanes can subgrid each other remains open in #14390.
    • Related: CSS Masonry, #10884, #12023, #14153, #14156
  • Scroll-driven animations get a first-class sticky range (#14181)
    • Background: scrollytelling effects often begin when a position: sticky element becomes stuck and end when it becomes unstuck. Authors can approximate this with view-timeline offsets, but must manually keep those offsets synchronized with sticky insets and surrounding layout.
    • Why it matters: animation-range: stuck turns a common multi-property calculation into an author-facing state. It makes sticky chapter transitions, pinned horizontal scrollers, and other scroll effects less fragile under responsive layout changes.
    • Summary: the group resolved to start specifying animation-range: stuck (resolution). The minutes favored a range rather than a new timeline because authors may want a transition from the stuck point into another existing range. The first follow-up immediately found unresolved semantics: an element constrained at both edges can have two disjoint stuck intervals, suggesting stuck-start and stuck-end, and a non-sticky subject may need an inactive range. Other Interop-facing work fixed progress-timeline behavior at animation-range boundaries (#12134); fixed-position view-timeline subjects remain undefined in #14296.
    • Related: Scroll-driven Animations, #13608
  • line-clamp reverses course on hidden text for assistive technology (#12859)
    • Background: the group had resolved in February that clamped-away content should be absent from both visual rendering and screen readers. Accessibility feedback then highlighted low-vision users who combine enlarged text with VoiceOver or HoverText: zoom can leave them with only a few visible words even when the full text is present in the DOM.
    • Why it matters: line clamping is common in cards, tables, and “read more” previews. Whether hidden lines remain focusable, searchable, selectable, and exposed through accessibility APIs can determine whether content is merely visually shortened or genuinely unavailable.
    • Summary: the August discussion found conflicting author intents—sometimes clamping is presentational, sometimes it intentionally hides a long article—but rejected making the accessibility tree diverge from focus and selection behavior. The new resolution makes line-clamp behave like overflow-y: clip, with follow-up actions for accessibility review and documentation (resolution). This reverses February's hidden-content rule and aligns exposure with the current overflow model. Rendering details also converged around existing overflow behavior, including one-axis clipping around rounded corners (#14067 resolution).
    • Related: #14047, #13670
  • East Asian punctuation trimming expands from presets to composable controls (#13789)
    • Background: text-spacing-trim used a short list of compound values, each controlling several distinct operations: punctuation at paragraph starts, wrapped line starts, line ends, and adjacent punctuation runs. Even internationalization specialists reported that the presets were difficult to remember and could not express every combination.
    • Why it matters: this property controls whether Chinese and Japanese punctuation leaves unwanted half-em gaps at line boundaries. More explicit values let publishers choose typography for their language and house style instead of accepting a bundled preset.
    • Summary: the group adopted an expanded syntax that combines start, end, and adjacent-punctuation controls while retaining compound keywords, plus auto (resolution). The landing is not clean: the resolution pointed to syntax in the IRC log rather than quoting it, and the issue's i18n reporter immediately questioned whether the adopted form had received enough review and whether adjacent-punctuation behavior belongs in a separate property. The direction—expose the constituent controls—is set; names and grouping may still move.
    • Related: #14345, css-text-4

Still contested

  • #14143 top-layer :hover / :active propagation — August's test case confirmed that events, :hover, and :has(:hover) expose different trees; the August 20 telecon still did not resolve whether an open <select> should remain hovered.
  • #14125 detecting an installed application context — CSSWG prefers extending display-mode so it can match an application context and fullscreen simultaneously; Web App Manifest participants question whether that represents “installed” rather than merely “displayed like an app.”
  • #5292 inherited background color — customizable controls need a usable page background, but currentBackgroundColor, an inherited canvas-color, and reuse of accent colors have different transparency and naming problems; the August 26 call produced no resolution.
  • #14307 :has-slotted and fallback content — aligning with assignedNodes({flatten:true}) would count fallback content, but doing so consistently across nested slots risks shadow-tree encapsulation leaks.
  • #14266 base URL for CSS-defined URL patterns — document-relative patterns fit application routing, but make external stylesheet parsing depend on the embedding document and can expose URL components; origin-relative matching is the leading fallback.
  • #14079 weighted random-item() values — the capability is wanted, but percentage-first versus value-first syntax and colon/comma grouping remain open.

Publishing & spec status

  • CSS Color 4 published a new Candidate Recommendation Draft on August 25, while CSS Fonts 4 published a Working Draft the same day.
  • CSS Fonts 5 published a Working Draft on August 11.
  • The text stack moved together on August 14: CSS Text 3 published a Candidate Recommendation Draft and CSS Text 4 published a Working Draft.

---

entry.title: This month in CSSWG (July 2026)
entry.content:
This month in CSSWG

July was a design-debate month more than a resolution month: five telecons (July 1, 8, 15, 22, 29) produced twenty-one resolutions plus two async — including a brand-new :nav-source pseudo-class, flip-self-* keywords for the <select> picker, and a compat-driven revert of the flex shorthand's omitted basis to 0% — but the arcs that matter to developers played out in threads: the customizable <select> hover model got reopened, CSS mixins grew a hygiene/privacy design, and border-shape hit the "is this the right primitive?" wall. Scroll-driven animations, meanwhile, had a quietly productive Interop-2026 cleanup, and the July 29 telecon closed the month by pinning down long-open value and scroll-snap edge cases.

Notable this month

  • Customizable <select>: the :hover top-layer rules are back on the table (#14143)
    • Background: an earlier resolution made :hover/:active chains break at top-layer boundaries, so a <select> stops looking hovered while its picker is open. emilio reopened it: native selects don't behave that way, and the model is inconsistent with how mouseenter/mouseleave work.
    • Why it matters: this decides whether the button of a customizable <select> can visually react while the picker is open — a styling question every adopter of customizable select hits. WebKit already ships the current behavior; Gecko doesn't yet, so the window to change it is closing.
    • Summary: a genuine cross-vendor split, no resolution. jakearchibald showed that even a custom <button> can't receive hover styles and wished the select button were a sibling pseudo-element; josepharhar defended the current magic (authors shouldn't need :not(:open) everywhere); mfreed7 framed top-layer elements as "pretend they're the last child of <body>", to which emilio countered that the pretence is rendering-only — events and selection don't play along. The July 9 telecon punted (dbaron wanted Mason Freed present). In parallel, jakearchibald proposed a better default height for the picker, which josepharhar supports — he had earlier called Chrome's current min-block-size a mistake — while fantasai pinned down the core problem: max-block-size: stretch resolves against the position-area-restricted containing block so the picker never flips when expected, and proposed calc(100svb - 8px) instead. The picker's positioning did land something concrete: July 1 RESOLVED to add flip-self-inline/flip-self-block to position-try and use them for ::picker(select), so the picker flips using its own writing mode.
    • Related: Anchor Positioning, #11838 (field-sizing: content in the base-appearance stylesheet), #13541 (June's position-fallback groundwork)
  • CSS mixins: @locals hygiene design, and whether @mixin survives as a name (#14004)
    • Background: custom functions and mixins are both in the css-mixins-1 draft (the original umbrella proposal was closed as accepted this month). LeaVerou proposed making today's pseudo-private --_var convention real: an @locals block whose variables are hygienically rewritten in place, private without a dummy mixin.
    • Why it matters: this is the "Sass features, natively" wave. Whether component libraries can actually hide internals — from the cascade, from devtools enumeration, from JS — decides how useful native mixins are compared to preprocessors.
    • Summary: the direction has broad support and the month hammered out its semantics: tabatkins wants the local properties themselves hidden but is fine exposing the rewritten (unguessable) names; Lea flagged devtools-style enumeration as a leak and wants @locals at the sheet top level too; kbabbitt models locals as hoisted secret-name declarations; keithamus asked for minifier-elision guarantees. The naming stakes surfaced in #13727: with these adopted, tabatkins says the separate @mixin rule could be dropped entirely; Lea insists @macro should go instead — @mixin is the term of art. Ergonomics kept moving: parameter-less mixins now serialize without parentheses (async RESOLVED, July 27), !important was declared invalid in function/mixin parameters, and comma-separated @apply lists were rejected for conflicting with contents blocks.
    • Related: #12417 (where @mixin may appear), #14007
  • border-shape growing pains: what strokes a custom border? (#13506)
    • Background: the single-shape border-shape takes its stroke width and color from one border side's properties. For shapes like una's scalloped cards — a 2px stroke on a ~20px-deep shape — that coupling forces padding hacks, so noamr proposed border-shape-stroke-* override properties.
    • Why it matters: corner-shape/border-shape is the new fancy-borders surface and has shipped in only one engine — the design is still movable, and how it lands decides how far CSS borders go toward SVG-style stroked drawing.
    • Summary: the July 8 telecon discussed it without resolving, and the thread became the month's biggest design fight. Lea argued the recurring footguns call the whole primitive into question ("there is still time to completely redesign"); tabatkins countered that anything short of the full stroke property set (miterlimit and all) is incomplete; noamr floated border-style: stroke as the opt-in and tabatkins sketched how it would compose. Scope got trimmed around the edges: Lea proposed deferring the two-shape variant to L5 (noamr and tabatkins pushed back), the corner shorthand's slash-parsing worries mostly dissolved once kbabbitt dug up the earlier resolution, and the interaction with classic border properties got its own issue (#14149). Month-end, tabatkins queued the full stroke-property set for border-shape-* for discussion — the "all or nothing" position, now on the agenda.
    • Related: #14147 — an overflow-safe shape-inside hitting the same "shapes meet the box model" wall: cyclic sizing vs tabatkins' stretchy-shapes idea
  • Scroll-driven animations: an Interop-2026 alignment month (#11469)
    • Background: scroll-animations-1 and web-animations-2 edge cases are being flushed out by Interop 2026 test work, with WebKit and Gecko implementations catching up to Chromium's shipped behavior — see Scroll-driven Animations.
    • Why it matters: each of these changes observable Web Animations API behavior for anyone scripting scroll/view timelines — and they mark the spec converging on what can interoperably ship.
    • Summary: six resolutions landed. Setting rangeStart/rangeEnd to values that need an element to resolve is now a parse error (July 1); play() on a scroll-driven animation re-aligns a sticky start time to the scroll range (July 8); ViewTimelineOptions.inset defaults were settled as "spec is right, fix the tests", as was coordinated-value-list shorthand serialization (July 15); and auto-aligning a start time now applies a pending playback rate (async, July 20). And the ViewTimeline constructor now takes a non-optional dictionary with a required element (July 29) — the minutes record weinig framing it as an IDL contradiction (a non-nullable subject attribute you could nonetheless construct as null) and ydaniv noting a subject-less ViewTimeline is practically useless, so the constructor got stricter instead. Still moving: BorisChiou flagged the CSSKeywordish typing of inset as interop-blocking, named-timeline re-lookup timing is queued (#13944), and a fresh proposal asks how zoom interacts with animation-range.
    • Related: Scroll-driven Animations, #14205 (rangeStart/rangeEnd IDL fix)
  • Masonry (grid-lanes): filling in the corners, and the reading-order question returns (#13931)
    • Background: after the 2025-11 display: grid-lanes decision, spec work is now detail-filling — see CSS Masonry.
    • Why it matters: the details being decided now (gaps, gap decorations, out-of-flow behavior, reading order) are what will make masonry usable — or an accessibility hazard — when it ships.
    • Summary: the July 22 telecon resolved that static positions of out-of-flow items reverse under fill-reverse, following flexbox precedent. css-gaps opened a five-issue family defining how gaps and gap decorations work in grid-lanes containers (#14153, #14154, #14155, #14156, #14169). And the long-running accessibility thread on reading order woke up: tabatkins proposed a "reading region" algorithm approximating the reading flows implied by layout, rachelandrew found the rules sensible, and accessibility advocate nattarnoff returned to review the proposals.
    • Related: CSS Masonry, #10884 (item-slack naming), #13512 (grid-auto-flow: normal compat risk measured at ~3% of pageloads)
  • :nav-source: style the element that started a navigation (#11801)
    • Background: bramus proposed a pseudo-class for the element that initiated the outgoing navigation, mirroring the Navigation API's sourceElement; css-navigation-1 drafted it as a links-only :trigger-link.
    • Why it matters: unlike :active, this state stays on until the navigation completes — exactly what you need to keep the clicked card or link highlighted while a cross-document view transition is under way.
    • Summary: the July 1 telecon resolved twice: the pseudo-class applies not just to links (forms and submit buttons also trigger navigations), and it is named :nav-source.
    • Related: css-navigation-1 — a young module now carrying its first author-facing selector
  • ::first-line / ::first-letter won't apply inside text inputs (#13926)
    • Background: Blink half-accidentally supported ::first-line on input/textarea; the internal layout of form controls is unspecced and differs across engines, so behavior there was never interoperable.
    • Why it matters: an author-visible selector rule is now explicit: these pseudo-elements do nothing on text inputs, the same way ::before/::after don't apply — one less cross-browser surprise.
    • Summary: RESOLVED July 15: they don't apply "for now", to be revisited once form-control internals have defined layout. In the call, lea pressed the author-expectation side while emilio argued there's simply no interoperable layout to hook them onto.
    • Related: #14190 — the same "spec the form-control layout" push in reverse: making align-content center a block-container <button>'s content, with a Gecko prototype already up
  • flex: 1 means flex-basis: 0% again — the spec bows to compat (#5742)
    • Background: the flex shorthand's omitted basis was originally 0%, then respecified as 0 in 2015 — but implementations never followed, and the open question had been flagged on the feature's page since it was written up.
    • Why it matters: flex: 1 is on practically every flexbox on the web, and 0% and 0 behave differently in indefinite-main-size containers. The spec now matches what every engine actually does, so the longstanding "spec says 0, browsers do 0%" trap disappears.
    • Summary: RESOLVED July 29: switch the omitted flex-basis back to 0% for compat, with a spec note about it. The minutes record tabatkins summarizing the decade-long arc: 0% was chosen "specifically to trigger indeterminate behavior", the later 0px change was never adopted by implementations, and "at this point, we're fairly certain it can't be changed" — sites depend on 0%.
    • Related: the flex shorthand — July's /query page traced this exact history
  • calc-mix() learns to simplify like calc() (#13839)
    • Background: weinig hit missing simplification rules while implementing css-values-5's calc-mix() and proposed a set in the issue.
    • Why it matters: simplification is observable — it is what serialization and getComputedStyle() return — so this defines the first interop surface of the new mix notation before two implementations diverge.
    • Summary: RESOLVED July 29: calc-mix() simplifies exactly as calc() would, except the mixed-type case resolves to calc(0px + 0%). The minutes record tabatkins framing calc-mix() as a convenience for linear interpolation that should drop 0% terms the way calc() drops products — but never simplify away to nothing.
    • Related: css-values-5 — the module also carrying random() and sibling-index()
  • getComputedStyle() on view-transition pseudos that don't exist (#13904)
    • Background: engines disagreed on what getComputedStyle() should return for ::view-transition-* pseudo-elements that don't currently exist — a WPT test invented an inheritance tree, and Chrome crashed on some queries.
    • Why it matters: these pseudos are how view-transition authors debug; what a non-existent one reports is now defined instead of engine-dependent.
    • Summary: RESOLVED July 1: non-existing pseudo-elements inherit from their ultimate originating element when queried. Follow-ups settled an author concern — martrapp relied on non-existent pseudos reporting a non-px width, and emilio confirmed that doesn't change: width isn't inherited, and a boxless pseudo still reports auto.
    • Related: #14179 (scoped view transitions: async resolution proposed July 27 — startViewTransition throws for elements that can't have layout containment), #13428 (scoped-VT capture vs the a11y tree)
  • Scroll snap pins down its edge cases: single-axis scrollers, joined axes, fragmentation (#14018)
    • Background: the group previously resolved to allow true single-axis scrollers (one axis scroll, the other clip no longer coerced); specs that assumed "a scroller scrolls both axes" are being updated.
    • Why it matters: snap behavior in nested or one-axis scroller setups becomes predictable: a snap position now attaches, per axis, to the nearest ancestor that actually scrolls that axis.
    • Summary: RESOLVED July 22: "Snap positions affect the nearest ancestor scroll container in each axis they align to." The same telecon also resolved that coincident snap candidates tie-break in flat-tree order, so shadow-DOM slotting no longer changes which element you snap to. The July 29 telecon kept going: a keyword (name TBD) will opt into joined-axis snapping — snap to an element in both axes or not at all, where today the axes always snap independently (the minutes record flackr arguing that for a two-axis snap target "the intent is usually to snap to the element entirely, or not at all") — and fragmented snap targets snap their bounding box, with alignment adjusted (details TBD) to keep the element in view when it is bigger than the viewport, resolving what multicol WPT failures exposed.
    • Related: #13816 (July 8: scroll direction of inputs follows the element's direction, closed no change)

Still contested

  • #13980 how does ::interest-button turn on? — still open after June's reversal; LeaVerou returned with new arguments for showing the affordance where expressing interest is cumbersome; the July 9 telecon didn't resolve.
  • #10001 wildcard selectors for utility classes — LeaVerou pushes .foo-; Loirooriol and Crissov raise grammar and attribute-selector conflicts, and the wildcard-character bikeshed ( vs ? vs %) ran through month-end, with edge cases collected in a dedicated tracking issue; the adjacent @selector proposal (#14180) is drawing skepticism.
  • #14112 anchor positioning: what happens on scroll? — anchored elements left behind by scrolling; part of the Anchor Positioning story.
  • #3658 system-ui is undesired for some users — loud thread, demoted here: largely a Windows CJK platform-font problem (jfkthame: "simply a platform font bug").
  • #11310 should contentvisibilityautostatechange bubble? — a proposed async resolution stalled at month-end: Blink ships the event bubbling and vmpstr calls changing that a compat risk, while smaug---- wants consistency with toggle and other non-bubbling events; LeaVerou's rule of thumb: "would bubbling prevent more bugs than it would cause?"
  • #10804 incremental rollout plan for form controls — the "future new controls" section met its first concrete case: Microsoft put the switch attribute forward as a candidate, and lukewarlow strongly opposes a base-switch, arguing it drags the whole styled-controls question in with it.
  • css-color conversion-precision cluster — #14133 zero chroma for powerless hue, #14134 carrying-forward step order, #14070 omissible alpha in relative-color serialization, #14207 DeltaE OK2 — spec-internal precision work with little author-visible impact so far.

Publishing & spec status

  • TR moves: css-color-4 → CRD, refreshed twice (2026-07-17 and 2026-07-28); css-link-params-1 FPWD published (2026-07-14) — the FPWD resolved in June is now on TR, and Chromium has opened implementation tracking; month-end WD refreshes for css-color-5 (2026-07-31) and css-color-hdr-1 (2026-07-28).
  • Selectors 4 CR push (#12799): horizontal review is complete and an updated WD is being prepared; fantasai reviewed the changes at the July 22 telecon and noted css-syntax-3 should republish first so the an+b grammar links resolve; by July 30 svgeesus had brought the Syntax 3 changes section up to date to unblock publication.

---

entry.title: This week in CSSWG (2026-07-23)
entry.content:
This week in CSSWG

The 2026-07-22 telecon delivered five resolutions — scroll snap caught up with single-axis scrollers, masonry settled an out-of-flow question, and filter effects cleaned up two SVG-era leftovers — while the mixins @locals design and the utility-class wildcard selector had their busiest week yet.

Notable

  • Scroll snap learns about single-axis scrollers (#14018)
    • Background: the group previously resolved to allow true single-axis scrollers (one axis scroll, the other clip no longer coerced to hidden); specs written assuming "a scroller scrolls both axes" are being updated one by one.
    • Why it matters: snap behavior in nested or one-axis scroller setups becomes predictable — a snap position attaches, per axis, to the nearest ancestor that actually scrolls that axis, so a horizontal scroll-snap-type on a vertical-only scroller no longer swallows the snap.
    • Summary: RESOLVED: "Snap positions affect the nearest ancestor scroll container in each axis they align to" (vmpstr's proposal, flackr's wording). The same call also resolved that coincident snap candidates tie-break in flat-tree order rather than DOM order, so shadow-DOM slotting no longer changes which element you snap to.
    • Related: #13832
  • Masonry: out-of-flow items follow fill-reverse (#13931)
    • Background: in a grid-lanes container with fill-reverse, items fill from the end of the stacking axis — so where should the static position of an absolutely-positioned child land? See CSS Masonry.
    • Why it matters: one more layout detail of the incoming masonry feature nailed down, consistently with what flexbox already does under its reversals.
    • Summary: RESOLVED to reverse static positions in grid-lanes, following flexbox precedent; TabAtkins and emilio noted static positions outside block layout are near-useless, so consistency and implementation simplicity won.
    • Related: CSS Masonry
  • Filter effects: two SVG-era cleanups (#13949)
    • Background: SVG 1.1's <filter href> inheritance was accidentally dropped from the Filter Effects spec and, it turns out, barely implemented anywhere; separately, the filter region for CSS boxes referencing SVG filters was never defined, and engines diverged between border box and ink-overflow bounds.
    • Why it matters: the first makes the accidental removal official (only Firefox ever shipped it); the second stops engines from exposing undefined ink-overflow bounds — an interop and privacy-adjacent cleanup for anyone using SVG filters on HTML.
    • Summary: RESOLVED to drop the href attribute on <filter>, and to define the filter region as the border box (bounding client rects for split inlines) — smfr flagged authors may need to extend the region when descendants overflow.
    • Related: #13964

Also active

  • #14173 auto-aligned start times apply a pending playback rate — the async resolution proposed last week was accepted on July 20 (scroll-driven animations / web-animations-2, Interop 2026).
  • #14004 @locals hygienic rewriting — the busiest design thread of the week: LeaVerou wants @locals at the sheet top level for private variables, kbabbitt's mental model is "hoisted declarations with secret names".
  • #10001 wildcard selectors for utility classes — LeaVerou pushed .foo-* with future extensions sketched; grammar conflicts with existing attribute selectors remain the sticking point.
  • #14143 :hover / :active top-layer propagation — mfreed7 pointed back at the original resolution's rationale; emilio listed what that discussion never considered.
  • #12799 Selectors 4 toward CR — svgeesus pushing an updated WD incorporating horizontal review; css-syntax-3 likely republishes first.
  • #14192 / #14193 — AccentColor cycles (color: AccentColor; accent-color: currentColor), with LeaVerou proposing a general "resolve against the parent" design principle.
  • #13980 ::interest-button — mfreed7 surveyed design systems for existing "info icon" cow paths after the July 22 discussion.

entry.title: This week in CSSWG (2026-07-16)
entry.content:
This week in CSSWG

The 2026-07-15 telecon spent its three resolutions on interop housekeeping — two "spec is right, fix the tests" calls for scroll-driven animations and one genuinely author-facing ruling: ::first-line/::first-letter won't apply inside text inputs. Around it, the customizable <select> hover debate and the border-shape design threads kept running hot.

Notable

  • ::first-line / ::first-letter won't apply inside text inputs (#13926)
    • Background: Blink half-accidentally supported ::first-line on input/textarea; the internal layout of form controls is unspecced and differs across engines.
    • Why it matters: an author-visible selector rule is now explicit — these pseudo-elements do nothing on text inputs, the same way ::before/::after don't apply.
    • Summary: in the call, lea pressed the author-expectation side ("if they're using it they're expecting it to work") while emilio argued there's no interoperable internal layout to hook them onto — password-input internals, ::placeholder interactions, none of it is specced. RESOLVED: they don't apply "for now", to be revisited once these controls have better-defined layout.
    • Related: #14190 (the flip side: making align-content center a block <button>'s content — bfgeek and emilio converged on a proposal this week)
  • Scroll-driven animations: two "fix the tests" rulings (#11644)
    • Background: Interop-2026 test work keeps flushing out places where Chromium's shipped behavior and the spec disagree — see Scroll-driven Animations.
    • Why it matters: both affect the Web Animations API surface of scroll/view timelines: ViewTimelineOptions.inset defaults to auto (which opts into scroll-padding), and shorthand serialization of coordinated value lists stays as specced.
    • Summary: RESOLVED spec is right, fix the tests for the inset default (Chrome's empty-array default was a years-old accident), and RESOLVED spec is right, fix tests, add animated-value tests for the serialization question. A third fix is queued as an async resolution: auto-aligning a start time should apply a pending playback rate.
    • Related: Scroll-driven Animations, #13500

Also active

  • #14143 :hover / :active top-layer propagation — the customizable-<select> hover debate kept going all week (19 comments): mfreed7's "popovers pretend to be the last child of <body>" framing vs emilio's "that pretence is rendering-only" pushback.
  • #13506 stroking border-shape — converging on a possible border-style: stroke opt-in that unlocks SVG-style stroke properties; #14150 deferring two-shape border-shape to L5 got pushback from noamr and tabatkins.
  • #14190 align-content on a block <button> — fresh issue, and by week's end a concrete proposal with implementer buy-in from bfgeek.
  • #14004 @locals hygienic rewriting — tabatkins and kbabbitt working through whether rewritten variable names should ever be observable.
  • #14181 a stuck range name for sticky elements and #14188 zoom × animation-range — two fresh scroll-driven-animations proposals aimed at "scrolltelling" patterns.
  • Publishing: css-link-params-1 FPWD published (2026-07-14).

Agenda ahead

  • #14143 :hover / :active top-layer propagation (Agenda+, waiting on Mason Freed)
  • #14172 better default sizing for custom <select>
  • #14149 border-shape × classic border properties

entry.title: This week in CSSWG (2026-07-09)
entry.content:
This week in CSSWG

A quiet week: the 2026-07-08 telecon produced only two resolutions, and the one that matters to authors tightens how play() behaves on a scroll-driven animation. Everything else is freshly-opened issues — a forms control-value() umbrella and two smaller behavior questions — queued for the F2F rather than decided.

Notable

  • Scroll-driven animations: play() should re-align a running animation to its scroll range (#11469)
    • Background: a WPT subtest ("Playing a running animation resets a sticky start time") assumes that calling play() on a running scroll-driven animation whose start time was set explicitly should reset that start time (scroll-animations-1 / web-animations-2).
    • Why it matters: scroll-driven animations already ship in Chromium and are scriptable through the Web Animations API. Setting an animation's start/current time can push it out of alignment with the scroll range, and play() is the natural "re-sync" call — so its exact behavior is directly observable to anyone scripting a scroll or view timeline.
    • Summary: implementers noted in the call that Chrome already applies an auto-rewind/auto-align on play() that realigns the animation to the scroll range, which is slightly different from what the spec currently says. RESOLVED to change the spec to meet the comment in the issue, bringing the wording in line with that realign-on-play() behavior.
    • Related: web-animations-2, Scroll-driven Animations

Also active

  • #14143 reconsider the :hover / :active top-layer propagation rules — a fresh css-ui follow-up to the earlier resolution (#11185) that made :hover/:active break at top-layer boundaries, revisiting how that squares with mouseenter/mouseleave.
  • #14129 formalize the <event-trigger-event> value — replaces the currently placeholder value grammar in the new animation-triggers-1 spec.
  • #14140 control-value() meta issue — a new css-forms-1 umbrella tracking the control-value() work for form controls (Agenda+ F2F).
  • #13816 close no change — RESOLVED to close, with no change, a css-overflow-3 / css-writing-modes-4 question about scroll direction for content inside inputs.

Agenda ahead

  • #14140 control-value() meta issue (Agenda+ F2F)
  • #14143 :hover / :active top-layer propagation (Agenda+)

entry.title: This week in CSSWG (2026-07-05)
entry.content:
This week in CSSWG

One telecon (2026-07-01) produced six resolutions, clustered on forms and navigation ergonomics: anchor positioning grew self-flipping keywords wired into the <select> picker, and the navigation-source selector was broadened beyond links and named :nav-source. Picked for what changes authoring, not for what was loudest — the week's highest-comment threads were CSS Color 5 serialization minutiae, left to the "Also active" list.

Notable

  • Anchor positioning learns to flip against its own writing mode, and drives the <select> picker (#14062)
    • Background: position-try's existing flip-inline/flip-block flip using the containing block's writing mode; this follows on from #13541 and #13738.
    • Why it matters: ties anchor positioning to the customizable <select> picker (::picker(select)) — one of the most-watched author-facing surfaces right now — and adds in-place mirroring that doesn't depend on the container's writing mode.
    • Summary: RESOLVED to add flip-self-inline/flip-self-block to position-try and to use these values for ::picker(select) — fantasai raised the element's-own-writing-mode use case, TabAtkins +1, no objection.
    • Related: #13541, #13738, CSS Anchor Positioning
  • The navigation-source selector goes broader than links, and gets a name: :nav-source (#11801)
    • Background: the original :trigger-link was scoped only to <a>; the selector targets the element that initiated an outgoing navigation, mirroring the Navigation API's sourceElement.
    • Why it matters: cross-document view-transition and scroll-restoration styling gets a way to target "what the user activated" — and since forms/submit buttons initiate navigations too, a link-only selector would have nudged authors toward links where a form belongs.
    • Summary: RESOLVED it applies not just to links and to add a :nav-source pseudo-class; the name won over :trigger-link, though dbaron and bramus flagged that "source" could be misread as the page you came from.
    • Related: css-navigation-1, selectors-5
  • Web Animations makes element-dependent typed values a parse error (#13853)
    • Background: the setters for rangeStart/rangeEnd accept <length-percentage>, but relative units (and var(), sibling-index(), …) have no resolution context outside style resolution.
    • Why it matters: closes a footgun where a value that can only resolve against a live element was silently accepted; absolute lengths and percentages stay valid.
    • Summary: RESOLVED to make it a parse error to set string or typed CSSOM values that require an element to resolve — weinig, TabAtkins and fantasai chose reject-now, relax-later once a processing model exists.
    • Related: web-animations-2
  • View Transitions: what getComputedStyle returns for a pseudo-element that doesn't exist (#13904)
    • Background: prompted by a WPT that assumed a whole non-existent pseudo-element inheritance tree.
    • Why it matters: pins down observable behavior for tools and tests probing view-transition pseudo trees.
    • Summary: RESOLVED that non-existing pseudo-elements inherit from their ultimate originating element when you query the computed style — emilio and TabAtkins argued the engine shouldn't invent the state of a tree that isn't there.
    • Related: css-view-transitions-1, cssom-1

Also active

  • #5675 Masonry reading-order / accessibility — 17 comments; the long-running accessibility objection to Grid-integrated masonry, circling a "reading region" proposal — part of the CSS Masonry story.
  • #11469 scroll-animations: should play() reset the start time? — observable behavior for scroll-driven animations authors.
  • #13809 css-forms-1: accent-color and base appearance — how the customizable-controls work interacts with accent-color.
  • #13980 Should ::interest-button be opt-in, opt-out, or media-query-enabled? — 6 comments; how the interest-invoker pseudo turns on.
  • #12953 Scoped view transitions on a shadow root — 6 comments.

Agenda ahead

  • #14102 display: contents on replaced elements
  • #14097 hanging value for text-box-edge
  • #14098 grouping of <keyframe-block> declarations
  • #14100 css-color-5: Example 32 is outdated

entry.title: This month in CSSWG (June 2026)
entry.content:
This month in CSSWG

June's throughline was implementations catching up to specs, and specs reacting. Selected for developer impact rather than comment volume: the ::interest-button default reversed, scroll-driven animations got a semantics pass, Link Params reached FPWD, and randomness matured in Values 5 — while the loud-but-low-impact CSS Color 5 serialization threads are gathered under "Still contested." 28 resolutions landed across ~92 active agenda items.

Notable this month

  • ::interest-button reverses course on turning itself on (#13980)
    • Background: ::interest-button surfaces an affordance for interest invokers (interestfor). Early June RESOLVED to gate it behind an inline media condition (display: if(media())).
    • Why it matters: whether a layout-affecting control is on by default is a page-breaking decision for every author using interest invokers — a live cross-vendor question, not a detail.
    • Summary: after developer conversations at CSS Day, the group voided that resolution. LeaVerou argued authors would simply turn it off — anything that affects layout by default breaks pages, and an opt-out adds more UX noise (stray tab stops, tooltips among real targets) than it solves. How it turns on is open again (37 comments this month).
    • Related: UA-latitude vs. "layout-affecting defaults get disabled" — the tension to watch as interest invokers ship.
  • Scroll-driven animations get a semantics pass (#13817)
    • Background: several scroll/view-timeline timing rules were underspecified, producing "why did my scroll animation jump?" surprises.
    • Why it matters: these are exactly the edge cases authors hit wiring animations to scroll; the fixes change observable behavior.
    • Summary: RESOLVED — timeline-source changes apply asynchronously; auto-rewind has no effect when the timeline is unresolved with a new play-always trigger; startOffset/endOffset are nullable; scroll-timeline names are loosely matched.
    • Related: #13480, #13643, #13844, #13974, #13818
  • Link Params reaches First Public Working Draft (#14028)
    • Background: Link Params adds a param() function for parameterizing links/URLs.
    • Why it matters: a new spec crossing FPWD is the signal that a feature is officially on the standards track — worth a developer's radar.
    • Summary: RESOLVED to publish Link Params as FPWD and to require param() to carry at least two values.
    • Related: #13767
  • Randomness matures in Values 5 (#14079)
    • Background: CSS is gaining random()/random-item() and sibling counting; June nailed down evaluation rules.
    • Why it matters: new author-facing primitives — the syntax must be unambiguous before engines ship.
    • Summary: RESOLVED how random() evaluates inside arbitrary substitution and sibling-index()/sibling-count() failure behavior; random-item() weighting is still wrestling with a block 20% syntax overlap, leaning toward an if()-like pattern.
    • Related: #13662, #13736
  • Forms + anchor-positioning groundwork for customizable <select> (#13541)
    • Background: the customizable <select> work needs anchor-positioning primitives to place the picker.
    • Why it matters: this is the runway for July's flip-self-* keywords and ::picker(select) — the customizable-select story developers are watching.
    • Summary: RESOLVED to redefine the <select> position-try fallbacks and to give @position-try globally-scoped names like @keyframes.
    • Related: #13567

Still contested

  • CSS Color 5 serialization cluster — loud but low author-impact, demoted here: #14100 Example 32 outdated, #13996 color-mix() parsing, #13994 resolved value of alpha(), #14070 omissible alpha (no consensus).
  • #10579 static gamut-mapping algorithm — implementation results diverging (Firefox now implementing/benchmarking).
  • #5675 Masonry reading-order / accessibility — the long-running accessibility objection, part of the CSS Masonry story.

Publishing & spec status

  • Publishing: Link Params FPWD (#14028); republish Gaps L1 (#6900).
  • TR moves this month: css-color-4 → CRD, css-color-5 → WD, css-color-hdr-1 → WD, css-display-3 → CRD, css-text-3 → CRD, css-text-4 → WD, css-gaps-1 → WD, css-2026 → NOTE.
